message.reasoning_content:
Let me work through this carefully.

The position: $1,000 USDC in Gauntlet USDC Core MetaMorpho vault on Morpho, Ethereum. ~$40M TVL. The vault has allocated part of its liquidity to the wstUSR/USDC market (Resolv wstUSR collateral, LLTV 91.5%).

Timeline of events:
- 02:15: Vault totalAssets 39.74M, withdrawable 22.11M (55.6%). wstUSR/USDC allocation only 5,070 USDC. Market supply ~$10k, 79% utilized. Oracles normal.
- 02:21: 50M USR minted from 0x0 to an address in a single tx — huge, unbacked mint (later confirmed: attacker deposited 100k USDC and got 49.95M USR). This is the Resolv exploit.
- 02:23: 20M of the fresh USR deposited into wstUSR (wrapped). Morpho oracle unchanged.
- 02:31: Curve USR/USDC depegs: 0.77–0.88, then 0.69–0.72. Oracle vs market gap >25%.
- 02:38: Curve USR at 0.004–0.096 (~-97% vs peg). Oracle still 1.1330.
- 02:41: Analyst flags USR trading at one cent; 50M minted with $100k.
- 02:45: The vault (Gauntlet USDC Core) via public allocator reallocates INTO wstUSR/USDC market: ~2.59M supplied, borrowed against wstUSR collateral... wait, actually in Morpho, suppliers provide USDC and borrowers borrow USDC against wstUSR collateral. The "supplied/borrowed in same tx" pairs suggest the allocator moved vault liquidity into that market, and borrowers borrowed simultaneously. So the vault now has ~2.59M exposed to wstUSR/USDC market as USDC supplier, with wstUSR collateral backing loans at LLTV 91.5% (very high LTV allowed — collateral worth ~91.5% of loan can back it). The collateral is wstUSR which is backed by USR which is now worthless/unbacked.
- 03:00: wstUSR/USDC supply 4.91M, borrow 4.79M, utilization 97.5%. Vault holds 4.51M of it (11.3% of vault). Withdrawable 16.77M (42.2%). Curve USR ~0.74.
- 03:33: D2 Finance confirms exploit: attacker got 49.95M USR for 100k USDC (~$39M unbacked).
- 03:40: Utilization 100%, idle 0. Vault has 4.95M (12.5%) there. Withdrawable 17.31M (43.6%). Curve USR ~0.85 (bounced a bit?).
- 03:41: Another 30M USR minted to same address. Total 80.2M minted.
- 03:51: PeckShield security alert confirming multiple large mints.
- 04:00: Gauntlet sets wstUSR/USDC cap to 0 (curator response). But 4.95M already in the market stays; market 100% utilized. Vault withdrawable 14.83M (37.3%).
- 04:58: Resolv officially confirms exploit, paused all protocol functions, working on recovery.
- 05:00: Fluid idle USDC down 26.1M (flight of liquidity), fUSDC down 19M. Vault withdrawable 1.99M (5.0%), down from 14.83M at 04:00 — massive withdrawal run on the vault. 4.95M (12.5%) stuck in wstUSR/USDC at 100% utilization. Share price unchanged (no loss recognized yet).

So the situation: Resolv USR is exploited, ~80M unbacked USR minted. wstUSR (wrapped USR) is the collateral in the wstUSR/USDC Morpho market. The vault has 4.95M USDC supplied to that market (12.5% of vault assets), and the user has $1,000 in the vault, so ~$125 of the user's $1,000 is exposed to that market. The market is 100% utilized — suppliers cannot withdraw until borrowers repay or are liquidated. The collateral (wstUSR) is now backed by essentially worthless USR (trading at ~1 cent at one point). With LLTV 91.5%, borrowers borrowed up to ~91.5% LTV against wstUSR collateral. If wstUSR oracle still reads 1.1330 (stale/oracle not marking the depeg), then borrowers are NOT undercollateralized on-paper, so no liquidations occur, and bad debt will materialize when the oracle eventually marks down or when wstUSR becomes unredeemable (Resolv paused — redemptions halted).

Key mechanics: The borrowers borrowed 4.79M USDC against wstUSR collateral. That collateral is now worthless (USR unbacked, protocol paused). When the oracle updates to reflect reality, borrowers will be under water and liquidations will only recover a fraction; suppliers will face bad debt. The vault's 4.95M in that market is very likely to take a large loss — potentially near-total loss on that allocation (borrowers borrowed ~97.5% utilization; collateral is wstUSR which is a claim on USR... actually wstUSR is a staked/wrapped position that may include RLP insurance? Resolv's system: USR is backed by delta-neutral basis trade collateral; RLP is the junior insurance tranche. wstUSR is wrapped staked USR. The oracle reads wstUSR 1.1330. If USR itself is unbacked, wstUSR redemption value collapses).

Also note: the exploit means attackers minted 80M unbacked USR; they deposited 20M into wstUSR to use as collateral to borrow real USDC from Morpho markets. The attackers borrowed ~2.5M+ via 0xE08D… and more; total borrow 4.79M. The attackers' goal: extract real USDC using fake USR collateral. The suppliers (including this vault) are the victims. The 4.95M supplied by the vault is at extreme risk of near-total loss.

Meanwhile, the vault is facing a bank run: withdrawable dropped from 14.83M at 04:00 to 1.99M at 05:00 — depositors are pulling out en masse. The user's $1,000: only 5% of vault is withdrawable now. If the user wants to exit, they can only withdraw up to available liquidity pro-rata? In MetaMorpho/ERC-4626, withdrawals are limited by available liquidity; with a run, the user may not be able to withdraw fully now. The user's position: $1,000 total, ~$125 effectively stuck in the wstUSR market (12.5%), and the rest competing with a run on 1.99M withdrawable out of ~$40M... Actually withdrawable 1.99M vs totalAssets ~39.7M — but wait, totalAssets includes the stuck 4.95M. Withdrawable 1.99M means only 1.99M of USDC is idle/withdrawable across other markets. With $40M TVL and mass withdrawals ongoing, the queue will be long.

Hmm, but the user only has $1,000. Even so, if 35M+ of withdrawals are queued ahead, the user's withdrawal may not be executable now.

What action should the keeper take? Options: hold, reduce_light, reduce_to_target, exit, relever.

Risk level: This is a confirmed exploit of Resolv (the underlying protocol of the collateral in a market the vault is exposed to, 12.5% of vault assets), with the vault's funds stuck at 100% utilization, oracle stale, bad debt highly likely, and a bank run on the vault draining withdrawable liquidity. For the user's position: ~12.5% direct exposure to near-certain loss, plus liquidity risk on the remaining 87.5% (can't withdraw — only 5% withdrawable and a run in progress).

Risk: critical seems right. Confirmed exploit (official confirmation from Resolv itself, PeckShield alert, onchain evidence), direct exposure of the vault to the exploited asset's market, funds stuck, run on the vault.

Action: exit — withdraw/unwind the whole position now. But can they? The keeper can only propose an action; corridor limits enforce safety. Exiting means requesting withdrawal of the full $1,000. Given only 1.99M withdrawable and a run, an immediate full exit may be partially executable, but proposing exit is still the right move — get in the withdrawal queue / withdraw whatever is possible now. The alternative "reduce_to_target" doesn't make sense when the venue itself is compromised by a run and 12.5% is stuck. Exit is the defensive max.

Wait — is exit feasible/actionable? The instruction says "You cannot move funds, only propose an action; the corridor limits enforce safety." So we propose exit; the system will execute as feasible. Given a confirmed exploit touching the position's venue and a liquidity run, exit is correct. Even if partial, exiting now preserves what can be saved before the bad debt is recognized (share price still 1.1462 — no loss marked yet; first movers out at par, late movers eat the loss). This is the classic "run to the exit before losses are socialized" situation. The share price hasn't marked down the wstUSR exposure yet, so withdrawing now recovers ~full value pro-rata from remaining liquidity; waiting means the loss hits NAV and everyone's share price drops.

Actually, let me think about whether the user's $1,000 can even be withdrawn: MetaMorpho vaults — withdrawals can be requested and processed as liquidity becomes available; there's typically no queue in Morpho MetaMorpho v1 (withdrawals limited by idle liquidity; you can withdraw instantly up to available liquidity). With 1.99M idle and massive outflows, the user's $1,000 might still get out if they act fast — every second counts as others withdraw. So exit NOW is urgent.

Risk level: critical. Justification: confirmed exploit of Resolv (USR unbacked mint 80M), vault has 4.95M (12.5%) stuck in the wstUSR/USDC market at 100% utilization with stale oracle and near-worthless collateral → high probability of severe bad debt; vault under active bank run (withdrawable 14.83M → 1.99M in one hour); share price not yet marked down → exiting now preserves value; waiting risks loss on both the stuck 12.5% and inability to withdraw the rest.

Could one argue "high" instead of "critical"? The user's direct stuck exposure is 12.5% (~$125). But the liquidity run means the other $875 is also at risk of being unwithdrawable, and NAV loss will spread to all holders via share price once bad debt is realized. The vault's remaining markets are other Morpho USDC markets — presumably fine venues, but the run drains liquidity. Given confirmed exploit + direct exposure + run + stale oracle, critical is warranted. The scale: exploit ~$39M unbacked minted; vault exposure 4.95M with likely near-total loss on the 4.79M borrowed against fake collateral... Actually let's compute: borrowers borrowed 4.79M USDC against 20M+ USR-wrapped collateral. When oracle marks down, liquidations of wstUSR collateral will fetch ~nothing (USR at ~$0.01–0.85 fluctuating; wstUSR redemption paused). Suppliers bear the shortfall: up to ~4.79M bad debt against 4.91M supply → suppliers could lose ~97% of their supply in that market. The vault's 4.95M... wait vault holds 4.95M of the 4.91M supply? Numbers: at 03:00 supply 4.91M, vault holds 4.51M; at 03:40 vault has 4.95M (12.5%) — supply must have grown to ~5.4M or so. Anyway, vault holds most of the market supply. If borrowers default entirely, vault loses up to ~4.79M... but collateral liquidation might recover something if wstUSR retains any value (USR traded 0.69–0.88 at times; Resolv paused; recovery possible). Still, loss could be 50–100% of that market exposure.

For the user: $1,000 × 12.5% = $125 at near-total loss risk = ~12.5% of position; plus systemic run risk on the rest. Critical risk to the position overall given the venue is in a run and part is already stuck. I'd say critical.

Action: exit.

Reasons (short):
- Confirmed Resolv exploit: 80M unbacked USR minted (official Resolv confirmation + PeckShield + onchain).
- Vault has 4.95M (12.5%) stuck in wstUSR/USDC at 100% utilization; collateral (wstUSR/USR) now unbacked and protocol paused → severe bad debt likely on that sleeve.
- Oracle stale at 1.1330 vs market ~0.01–0.85 → no liquidations triggering, losses will hit suppliers suddenly.
- Bank run underway: vault withdrawable fell 14.83M → 1.99M (5%) in an hour; share price not yet marked down → withdraw now at par before loss recognition.
- Fluid/fUSDC liquidity also draining — broader flight.
